title: Raspberry Pi GPIO Pinout Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Every one of the 40 header pins, clickable, colour coded, with a safety line on each and a guided walkthrough of the four pins this book actually wires.

learningObjectives: Locate a specific pin on the 40-pin header by number and by function.
Identify which pins are safe to connect a 3.3 V sensor to.

keyQuestions: What is the difference between physical pin 3 and GPIO 3?
Which pins would you use to connect an I2C sensor, and why those?
commonMisconceptions: Confusing the physical pin number with the BCM GPIO number - they are different, and pin 3 is GPIO 2.
Assuming 5 V is "more power" and therefore better.
Believing there is only one correct ground pin.
assessmentOpportunities: Locates a pin by physical number and states its function.
Distinguishes physical pin numbering from BCM GPIO numbering.
Identifies the 5 V pins as the ones never to connect to a sensor or a GPIO pin.
